Package com.nexuslink.ui.files

Class DirectoryDiff

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.ui.files.DirectoryDiff
public final class DirectoryDiff extends Object
A single-level comparison of two directory listings — the "left" (e.g. local) pane against the "right" (e.g. remote) pane. Every entry is matched by name and classified as present on only one side, present on both but differing, or identical, which is what a commander needs to highlight new / changed / missing files and what SyncService (7.1) builds its plan from. The synthetic ".." row is ignored. Kept JavaFX-free so it is unit-testable, mirroring FileOrder and FileFilter.

      public static List<DirectoryDiff.Entry> compare(List<FileItem> left, List<FileItem> right, boolean caseSensitive)
      Compares two listings, matching entries by name (optionally case-insensitively for Windows-style filesystems). Neither input is modified. The result is ordered directories-first then case-insensitive name, matching how a commander lists a merged view.

    • compare

      public static List<DirectoryDiff.Entry> compare(List<FileItem> left, List<FileItem> right, boolean caseSensitive, DirectoryDiff.Match match, DirectoryDiff.Digests digests)
      Compares two listings, telling same-named files apart by match. For DirectoryDiff.Match.CONTENT, digests supplies each side's checksum; a typical caller diffs once by metadata, hashes only needsDigest(java.util.List<com.nexuslink.ui.files.DirectoryDiff.Entry>) entries, then re-compares with those digests.

    • needsDigest

      public static List<DirectoryDiff.Entry> needsDigest(List<DirectoryDiff.Entry> metadataDiff)
      The entries a DirectoryDiff.Match.CONTENT compare actually needs digests for: every same-named file pair of equal size, whatever the metadata verdict was. A differing size differs whatever the bytes say (no hash needed), but an equal size is undecidable from metadata alone — including a pair a stamp-based compare called SAME, since two byte-different files can share a size and a timestamp, and catching exactly that is why a content compare exists. So a caller hashes just these rather than every file in both listings.

      Pass the result of a DirectoryDiff.Match.METADATA compare; hash each entry's left/right and re-compare with DirectoryDiff.Match.CONTENT.
